title: Early galaxy evolution: The complex interstellar medium distribution of the z ∼ 7 galaxy A1689-zD1
question: Resolve the [CII] 158um and [OIII] 88um line and continuum structure and kinematics of the lensed z=7.13 galaxy A1689-zD1 at sub-kpc scales, decompose it into components, and compare line, SFR and mass properties with local and high-z relations

data.sensitivity: Band 6 cube 0.18-0.2 mJy/beam per 5 km/s channel, combined continuum 6.3 uJy/beam; Band 8 continuum 29 uJy/beam, cube 0.39-0.44 mJy/beam per ~11 km/s channel; Band 3 continuum 11 uJy/beam

what.value: Earlier ALMA continuum data combined with the lower-frequency Band 6 data

evidence.quote: When combining the lower frequency band with the continuum data from (cite: knudsen17)

what.value: Lenstool mass model of Abell 1689 used for magnification
Dust temperature of 41 K (spatially integrated best fit) fixed for the violet and red components

evidence.quote: $T_{\rm dust}=41$ K taken from the spatially integrated best-fit value presented in (cite: akins22)

what.value: NIR spectroscopic redshift from the Lyman break used for comparison

evidence.quote: the redshift derived from the NIR spectrum of the Lyman-break in (cite: watson15)

what.value: Flux scale for GBT absolute calibration with 3C286

evidence.quote: 3C286 was used for absolute flux calibration (cite: perley17)

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA Bands 3, 6, 8; subtract continuum
recipe.method: ALMA pipeline (Band 6) or observatory-delivered calibration (Bands 8 and 3); imaging with Briggs robust 0.5 (Band 6) or natural weighting with taper (Band 3); uvcontsub on [CII] and [OIII] cubes

recipe.goal: Derive systemic redshift from line centroids
recipe.method: Single Gaussian profile fit to each line; mean of the two redshifts as systemic redshift, difference as uncertainty
Parametric Lenstool mass model of Abell 1689 evaluated at the source position; statistical error from MCMC samples, systematic error from alternative mass models
key_parameters: Statistical relative error 19%; systematic relative error 10%
assumptions: No significant cluster substructure or cluster member near the source, so magnification varies by less than 10% across the source

recipe.goal: Decompose line cubes into spatial-spectral components
recipe.method: Iterative per-component procedure on the continuum-subtracted cubes: narrowband image, 2D elliptical Gaussian fit, 1D Gaussian spectrum fit, subtraction of a 3D model; repeated three times, with an arctan velocity-gradient model for extended components
key_parameters: Five components (violet, blue, green, yellow, red), blue and red each with two sub-components; components first identified in [CII] and recovered in [OIII]
Velocity gradients modelled with an empirical arctan model (truncation velocity and radius)
assumptions: Choice of decomposition is somewhat arbitrary and driven by data complexity and S/N; inclination fixed to 30 deg for all components (bracketed values are fixed)

recipe.goal: Decompose the dust continuum and derive dust temperature and L_IR per component
recipe.method: Forced-aperture photometry following the [OIII] component model, plus CASA imfit modelling with four components; modified blackbody with beta=1.7 to get T_dust and L_IR; T_dust fixed to 41 K for violet and red
key_parameters: Violet (red) component not fit in Band 6 (Band 8) maps; photometry taken in a 0.2'' radius aperture on the residual map; positions of faint components fixed, flux density free
assumptions: Single modified blackbody with spectral index beta = 1.7; T_dust = 41 K for violet and red

recipe.method: Sum of IR-based (obscured) and UV-based (unobscured) SFR using the ALMA and HST observations; UV luminosity measured in 0.2'' radius apertures, 3 sigma upper limits for components without HST counterparts
assumptions: Same IR and UV to SFR conversions as Akins et al., based on Murphy et al.

recipe.goal: Compare line luminosities, ratios and sizes with literature relations
recipe.method: Per-component and total L[CII], L[OIII], their ratio and SFR placed on SFR-L_line, SFR-L[OIII]/L[CII], Sigma_SFR-Sigma_[CII] and size-velocity dispersion diagrams alongside local and z>6 literature samples
key_parameters: Component sizes from 2D Gaussian FWHM of the model; effective radius taken as HWHM
assumptions: Plotted errors do not include size uncertainties

recipe.method: Disk formula (Dessauges-Zavadsky et al. 2020 Eq. 4) for the blue component, virial dispersion-dominated formula (Bothwell et al. 2013 Eq. 10) for the others, separately for [CII] and [OIII]; v_circ = 1.763 sigma_0 / sin(i) with i = arccos(FWHM2/FWHM1)
assumptions: Components may not be virialized, but estimates considered meaningful

evidence.quote: We obtain a statistical relative error of 19%

answer_key.quantity: Fraction of [CII] and [OIII] emission recovered by five components

evidence.quote: we recovered 95 and 97% of the total emission measured in the \[C ii\] and \[O iii\] line data, respectively
Correcting the data for gravitational magnification, the extracted components are found to have sizes in the range 0.1–1 kpc.

answer_key.quantity: Sum of five components' continuum flux density in Bands 6 and 8

evidence.quote: The sum of the five components gives $0.45\pm0.20$ mJy and $1.71\pm0.58$ mJy in bands 6 and 8, respectively.
obtain a total SFR of $16.5_{-6.8}^{+22}\,M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$
with a summed dynamical mass about $1.5\times10^{10}\,M_\odot$

answer_key.quantity: Total dynamical mass of the galaxy (abstract)

evidence.quote: The total dynamical mass of the galaxy ($2\times10^{10}$ M$_\odot$)

score_reason: Project codes and calibrators are given and key results (line luminosities, redshift, component parameter tables) are numeric, but imaging parameters, CASA versions and the fitting details of the decomposition are missing.
rediscovery_reason: The two ALMA projects are named and the headline numbers (redshift, L[CII], L[OIII], component tables) can be re-derived, though exact values depend on unstated imaging and fit settings.
